title: Loom model card measurements (info.json), schema loom-card/3
description: The data of a loom-fun card that has no other home: per GPU (devices): measurements, gate evidence, the device and Loom SDK that measured, the baseline, dates and versions. What the package is comes from its own files and is never repeated here: sources, revisions, files, sha256 and sizes from model.json.lock; services, context, rows, max_tokens and drafting depth from model.json; chat features, the drafter and the generating loom-skills commit and SDK from llm_config.json. render_card.py renders README.md from all four. Unknown values are null or absent (rendered as not measured / no evidence / unknown), never guessed.
$comment: Compatibility: the schema string changes only on a breaking change. Readers ignore metric names, gate names and object keys they don't know (the retired gates needle and needle_full stay valid in old files; make_info.py build drops them, card_lib.RETIRED_GATES), so adding a metric, a gate, an optional key or a new enum value of source.kind keeps loom-card/3. Removing or renaming a key, changing a key's type or meaning, or making a key required is breaking and bumps the schema to loom-card/4. loom-card/3 moved gates, performance and roofline under devices.<gpu>; loom-card/2 cards read as the strix-halo device (card_lib.normalize).

repo.description: The Hugging Face repo of this card

card.description: Choices about the card itself that no package file records

license.description: The checkpoint's license tag (from its Hugging Face card at publish time)

tags.description: Front matter tags after the ones the package implies

output.description: loom-fetch --output directory, when not model.json's model id

memory_bytes.description: loom-serve --memory_bytes the card was validated with, when model.json carries none

carried.description: How a GPU's rows and gates measured on another hrx-loom version than the card's Quick start installs are shown (the policy for GPUs without a DevLab runner). mark (default): shown, each marked with the SDK it was measured on, not re-qualified; drop: not shown (the GPU keeps its Quick start and a line saying so)

features.description: Every feature row as the card shows it, so a reader needs no other file: status yes, no (the upstream model has it, Loom lacks it), n/a (the upstream model has none) or unknown (not determined; rendered as a neutral ?, never red), and its value (speculative_decoding yes with a null method: a drafter is available upstream but not enabled). Written by make_info.py build from the package, the upstream model (vision, audio, chat template), the sampling gate and evidence (an old report stating greedy-only decoding); render_card.py shows these over what it derives itself

card_generator.description: loom-skills commit of the card scripts that wrote this info.json and its README ('unknown' if not a git checkout); passed in, never read by the renderer from the environment

package.description: Only for a package built before build.py stamped llm_config.json 'generator': what generated its programs, as recovered afterwards. Ignored when llm_config.json has the stamp.

sources.description: Where evidence came from, by id (referenced by performance sessions and gates)

devices.description: Per GPU, keyed by id (card_lib.GPUS). Added in loom-card/3: loom-card/2 held gates, performance and roofline at the top level, which readers take as the strix-halo entry (card_lib.normalize).

report.description: REPORT.md in the repo: generated by render_card.py from this file, or attached as written (an older card's narrative report, a factory run's REPORT.md)

status.description: Where work on this model stands, when not active: paused (work stopped; the card shows what was reached). Optional key, loom-card/2.

next_steps.description: What would be done next if work continued, one short markdown line each; README.md ends with them under Next steps. Optional key, loom-card/2.

gpu.description: What the card records for one GPU: measurements, gate evidence, roofline and how the package is served on it. A GPU without results carries a state.

state.description: not_measured: this package has no results on this GPU yet (the card says so and shows no numbers). unsupported: the package does not fit this GPU (required_bytes; the card says so). not_a_target: the package's format has no fast path on this GPU's family, so it is not measured there (reason; the card says so). Absent: the GPU has results.

reason.description: not_a_target only: why the GPU is not a target of this package

required_bytes.description: unsupported only: the memory the package needs on this GPU (weights, KV cache at the native context, headroom)

memory_bytes.description: loom-serve --memory_bytes on this GPU when it differs from the package value (model.json or card.memory_bytes): the GPU memory bounds the elastic pool

served_context.description: Tokens per request this GPU serves when its memory budget holds less KV cache than the native context needs; the same package serves it, --memory_bytes bounds the pool. Absent: the native context.

serve_args.description: The loom-serve flags this GPU is served with for this package (fleet/devices data file: its measured memory budget, state slab ...); they replace the GPU's registry flags in the Quick start. Present (even empty) on a GPU whose data file says the package fits, so the card shows its Quick start block before any performance row exists.

quick_start.description: How the card's Quick start serves the package on this GPU: the preset loom-fetch takes, the loom-serve --device URI and every other loom-serve flag after --model. Present on each GPU the card shows a Quick start for.

preset.description: The model.json preset to serve (loom-fetch REPO:PRESET, loom-serve --preset); null when the package has none

device.description: The loom-serve --device URI; a launcher that selects its own GPU keeps this URI's query (the completion wait the performance rows are measured with)

args.description: The loom-serve flags after --model and --device, in order, unquoted

shares_section_with.description: A GPU whose performance section this GPU shares (the same programs on the same silicon): the card prints one section headed with both names and no table of its own (fleet/devices flag share_section_with).

remeasure.description: A same-runner A/B (make_info.py remeasure, from strix_ab_compare.py) that re-measured this GPU on this package against the build whose performance sessions the card shows: every card metric within +-band. Sessions measured on compared_programs then stand for programs_sha256 (not marked as another build); the card says so in one line. Optional key.

programs_sha256.description: card_lib.programs_sha256 of the package re-measured (this repository's)

compared_programs.description: programs_sha256 of the build compared with (the sessions shown)

proof.description: result identical: the default-path stages of this package are identical to the compared build's after canonicalization (fleet/stage_equiv.py), so the performance sessions measured on compared_programs stand for this package without a re-measure; band is 0

carried_programs.description: result identical: the programs_sha256 of every build whose evidence (performance sessions, gates) the proof covers: compared_programs and, when that build was itself re-measured against the sessions' build, that one

previous.description: result identical: the re-measure block of the compared build (same keys), kept so the card still says how its table was re-measured

bands.description: the per-row bands (methodology.json) the comparison judged each row against

first_source.description: improved: the source of the first of the two runs that confirmed the faster rows (source is the second)

improved.description: rows faster than the published value in both runs: the card shows the mean of the two runs' medians for them, llama.cpp unchanged

exceptions.description: metrics outside the band in this run whose confirming run did not repeat it in the same direction (the card names them)

name.description: The engine compared with, e.g. llama.cpp

args.description: The exact server arguments (model path, host and port left out)

differs.description: Notes the card must show: a cell llama.cpp cannot run (not supported, with the reason) or a Loom-side limitation, one line each

baselines.description: Further llama.cpp backends measured with the same workloads, by backend name (vulkan: the official ggml-org release). Optional key, loom-card/2. Never a headline value or a guardrail input (card_lib.card_metrics reads sessions only); rendered as another backend column.

args.description: The exact server arguments (model path, host and port left out)

sha256.description: sha256 of the release archive the measurement ran

model.description: Another engine running ITS OWN model file (not the card's GGUF), e.g. Gufo on unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL: shown on the card; such a column is never the margin's baseline

differs.description: Server settings that differ from the main baseline's or that this backend could not run, with the reason, one line each (never silently changed)

session.description: One baseline-only measurement session (the latest replaces the earlier one); metrics hold the engine's value and per-run values only

aggregate.description: as session.aggregate; absent: the mean of the runs

programs_sha256.description: card_lib.programs_sha256 of the package the run fetched (its GGUF, drafter and settings came from it)

sessions.description: Measurement sessions in evidence order. Per metric the last session that measured it is the card's value (card_lib.card_metrics).

admission.description: The native-context admission check of the latest gates run on this GPU (gates.sh context_admit, ctx_admit.py): one request filling the context the GPU serves, admitted or refused

gates.description: Per gate name the most recent evidence. Gates the package's features make applicable but that have no entry render as no evidence.

roofline.description: The hardware ceiling of each performance metric, computed from the GGUF by loom-roofline's roofline.py (make_info.py roofline). Added in loom-card/2 (optional key).

bandwidth_bytes_per_s.description: memory bandwidth the decode ceilings divide by

peak_flops.description: FLOP/s the prefill ceilings divide by: the spec-sheet peak, or the measured sustained rate at power_mode

power_mode.description: the platform power mode peak_flops was measured at (e.g. "85 W"); absent: the spec-sheet peak

spec_peak_flops.description: the spec-sheet peak FLOP/s, kept for reference when power_mode is set

script.description: the script, relative to the loom-skills checkout

skills_commit.description: loom-skills commit of the checkout ('unknown' if not a git checkout)

checkpoint.description: the GGUF file the ceilings were computed from

oneOf.description: drafted rows (decode, 4 streams): ceiling = verify passes per second x tokens_per_pass = 1 + acceptance x depth; the drafter's own passes are not counted (an upper bound)

acceptance.description: the spec gate's acceptance (the card's spec_acceptance) when computed: the fallback for drafted rows whose session recorded no acceptance of its own

kind.description: local: a developer's machine (gates; performance at a named power_mode with every engine re-measured); machine: a named machine outside DevLab (fleet/devices results for a GPU without a DevLab runner); devlab: a workflow on AMD DevLab Dispatch; factory: the loom-factory workflow; xsj: an XSJ lab run on a leased host of a compatible runner-free registry device

run.description: GitHub Actions run ID, or for kind xsj the XSJ lab run ID (YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-xxxx)

hrx_loom.description: The Loom SDK that served the model

conclusion.description: devlab/factory: the GitHub Actions conclusion of the cited job, when recorded; render_card.py refuses a card citing a job that did not succeed

power_mode.description: local only: the platform power mode the job ran at (a key of the device preset's power_modes, e.g. 123w); a local source with it may hold performance (card_lib.perf_source_ok, methodology rule 18)

power.description: local only: power_steps.json summary: per engine median W / GHz of busy samples, steps outside the band

device.description: Recorded hardware and OS. For an XSJ source all six fields are required; host is the pool alias and arch is the registered gfx ID.

hrx_loom.description: A Loom SDK identity: install_loom.sh's loom-install.json, or version + dist-info RECORD fingerprint
The package version (a release reports its own version, e.g. 0.2.0rc1; 0.1.0 and earlier CI builds all said 0.1.0)

source.description: release (a GitHub release: 0.2.0rc1), pypi or ci

fingerprint.description: First 16 hex of sha256(dist-info RECORD) when nothing better is known

recovered.description: Established after the fact rather than recorded at the time

basis.description: How a recovered value was established

no_generator.description: programs no loom-skills generator made (a hand-written package): commit null, basis says so

decode_prefill.description: sessions per decode/prefill value ("aggregate": "median"), else runs averaged (mean)

samples.description: metric -> samples per session, for the rows measured several times within a session (perf.py --repeat-rows); the other rows have one

aggregate.description: how the session's values were made: the MEDIAN over serve sessions (rounds) of each session's median sample (methodology rule 5). Absent: the session was measured as the mean of runs.decode_prefill rounds (4 streams: median of runs.streams4); never relabelled

over_context.description: metric -> prompt tokens (null: not counted) of a long document the Loom server refused as over its context (make_info.py perf; card_lib.over_context)

loom_runs.description: per-session values (per-run in a session without aggregate; 4 streams: its runs) the card value summarizes

baseline_from.description: Present when this row's llama.cpp value was measured in another job than the Loom value (a Loom-only job, make_info.py perf --baseline-from-info): the date and source id of the session that measured it. Absent: both come from this session (the same job).

acceptance.description: speculative decoding: accepted / proposed drafted tokens of this metric's own Loom requests (median over the sessions of each session's median, mean of the runs in a session without aggregate; perf.py, c4_steady.py), the acceptance its roofline ceiling counts

accepted_per_pass.description: spec_acceptance with unreported proposals: drafted tokens accepted per verification pass (accepted / (decode_tokens - accepted) from loom-serve's counters; bench_common.per_pass_between), measured without the draft depth

unreported.description: spec_acceptance only, with loom null: proposals = the SDK counted accepted drafted tokens but no proposals for this package's controller (hrx-loom 0.3 with a service ABI 1 controller; bench_common.proposals_unreported); never derived from the configured draft depth

level.description: gates.sh LEVEL the evidence ran at

detail.description: a count from the gate's own output (e.g. 66/66), or null

ceiling.description: tokens per second at the hardware limit (null: not computable, e.g. a drafted row without acceptance)

single_pass.description: the ceiling without speculative decoding (drafted rows only)

efficiency.description: the fraction of the ceiling tuned Loom ports have demonstrated for this kind of metric (roofline.py EFF / EFF_DRAFTED); the far-from-roofline guardrail compares against it

acceptance.description: drafted rows: the acceptance this ceiling counts

acceptance_from.description: session: measured in the same session as the card's value of this row; spec_gate: the spec gate's (its text can accept more or less than the row's)

basis.description: mixture-of-experts 4-stream row: the ceiling assumes the four streams route to the same experts (the hard bound a run may not exceed)

value.description: structured detail the renderer formats (string, number, object or null)
